items.title: Khandre pulls up JJM engineers over lack of knowledge on water budgeting
points: Minister for Rural Development and Pannchayat Raj Eshwar Khandre presiding over a progress review meeting at the zilla panchayat in Mysuru on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: M.A.
Sriram Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar B.

Khandre pulled up Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) engineers for their lack of knowledge about water budgeting after they failed to explain the concept during a progress review meeting at the Mysuru Zilla Panchayat office here on Wednesday.
“What is water budgeting?” was the question posed by the Minister to the engineers.
Officials should also assess whether surface water sources would be sufficient to provide safe drinking water to rural households over the next 30 years and plan projects accordingly, he said.

Pointing out that the State government was spending ₹67,000 crore on multi-village and single-village drinking water schemes, Mr. Khandre questioned the purpose of such huge investments if water failed to reach households.

items.title: Rural polls to kick off in three districts amid heightened security on November 5
points: With polling scheduled from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., the three districts remain fully geared up for a crucial grassroots electoral exercise amid heightened security in the backdrop of the region’s political rivalry and past faction feuds.
The three districts have 84 ZPTC and 1,087 MPTC seats across 84 mandals.
Chittoor accounts for 27 ZPTC and 370 MPTC seats, with 10.26 lakh voters.
Annamayya has 25 ZPTC and 321 MPTC seats and 9.09 lakh voters, while Sri Sathya Sai has 32 ZPTC and 396 MPTC seats with 11.35 lakh voters.
Three ZPTC seats each in Chittoor and Annamayya were reported elected unopposed, leaving 78 ZPTC seats for polling across the region.
In 2021, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) trounced the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and won the Zilla Parishad chairmen posts of combined Chittoor, Anantapur and Kadapa districts.
“Chittoor has 1,236 polling stations, including 366 sensitive and 346 highly sensitive centres, with around 2,000 police personnel earmarked for election security,” he said.

items.title: Pangappara Abhiram murder case: police suspect double murder plot
points: Published - November 04, 2026 09:25 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Thiruvananthapuram City police investigating the murder of 17-year-old Abhiram in Pangappara suspect that the accused had initially planned a double murder.
According to the police, the murder was part of a premeditated conspiracy that was allegedly aimed at killing both Abhiram and another person.
However, the second intended victim, Abhiram’s friend, was not brought to the location.
The 17-year-old prime accused was allegedly motivated by resentment towards his former girlfriend, who had reportedly become close to Abhiram’s friend.
A 16-member special investigation team has been formed to probe the case.

The investigation is being led by the Sreekaryam Circle Inspector under the supervision of an Assistant Commissioner of Police, Cyber City, with cyber experts assisting in the examination of digital evidence.

Meanwhile, the District Police Chief (Thiruvananthapuram City) has submitted a report to the Additional Director General of Police, Law and Order, stating that there was no lapse on the part of the police in handling the case.

items.title: Telangana Tourism showcases heritage and culture at WTM London 2026, seeks global spotlight
points: Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated the Telangana Tourism Pavilion at the three-day international tourism exhibition, being held at ExCeL London in the United Kingdom from November 3 to 5.

Among the prominent destinations being highlighted are the Ramappa Temple, Warangal Fort, Thousand Pillar Temple, Golconda Fort, Charminar, Nagarjunasagar, Buddhavanam, Ananthagiri Hills, Laknavaram Lake, Bogatha Waterfalls and the Kaleshwaram region.

The pavilion also positions Hyderabad as an international destination for heritage tourism, gastronomy, shopping, entertainment, medical tourism and Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE).

“The Telangana delegation is using the three-day event to hold business-to-business meetings, destination presentations and networking sessions with international tour operators, travel agents, destination management companies, airlines, hospitality groups…

The engagements are aimed at attracting international visitors, exploring tourism investment opportunities and establishing strategic partnerships, particularly in the United Kingdom and European markets,” said an official.

They added that the State is also seeking to promote lesser-known destinations, develop customised tourism circuits and explore international collaborations in heritage, cultural, spiritual, nature-based and experiential tourism.

items.title: Bengaluru: Man arrested for cheating woman of gold, silver ornaments worth ₹17 lakh near Bagalur
points: The complainant, Pushpa T., 40, a resident of Devli town in Tonk district of Rajasthan, lodged a complaint at the Bagalur Police Station on October 14.
According to the complaint, the woman had visited the Yeshwanthpur Railway Station on October 14 to purchase a ticket to travel to Rajasthan.
An unidentified man approached her, claiming that he could arrange a flight ticket at a lower rate.
The accused then took her near Mayura Bakery in the Bagalur area.
The Bagalur police registered a case and began an investigation.
The police traced and arrested the accused, identified as Chanuvar Ali, 36, on October 15 in Ganga Nagar.
The police have recovered 117.33 grams of gold ornaments and 71.83 grams of silver jewellery from him.
The recovered valuables are estimated to be worth approximately ₹17 lakh.

items.title: Andhra CM Chandrababu Naidu seeks relief package for drought-hit farmers
points: The State has declared 412 mandals across 21 districts drought-affected and is expected to submit a report on crop losses to the Centre within a week. | Photo Credit: File Photo Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N.

Chandrababu Naidu has sought a relief package for drought-hit farmers, which includes 200 days of employment under the VB-G RAM G scheme, ration cards for eligible affected families, rescheduling of agricultural loans and faster settlement of crop…
The team had visited Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai districts on November 2 and 3 to assess the drought situation.
Mr. Naidu said deficient rainfall and prolonged dry spells severely affected kharif crops.
The State had declared 412 mandals across 21 districts drought-affected and would submit a report on crop losses to the Centre within a week, he said.
Mr. Naidu wanted the minimum guaranteed employment under the VB-G RAM G scheme increased to 200 days and its scope extended to agricultural activities as well.

items.title: Power to revoke licences used sparingly, Kerala HC expresses dissatisfaction at MVD inaction
points: Despite statutory provisions in place, Motor Vehicles department authorities only disqualify or revoke licences sparingly, observed the Kerala High Court while deciding a bail application in a drunk driving case.

“At a time when incidents of drunk driving continue to claim precious lives and leave families devastated, it is imperative that the authorities exercise the powers conferred under the Motor Vehicles Act (MV Act) with the seriousness that the situation…

Justice Kauser Edappagath directed the Transport Commissioner to ensure that prompt and effective action is taken under the Act in cases of drunk driving, where a road accident is prima facie caused by the driver’s state of intoxication.
The licensing authority should act swiftly and consider initiating proceedings to disqualify or revoke the driving licence involved.
The court noted that instances of road traffic accidents due to drunk driving were a matter of serious and growing concern.

items.title: Guwahati hotel shooting case: Prime accused killed in police ‘encounter’
points: The prime accused in the October 26 Guwahati hotel shooting, which killed five, was shot dead in an alleged police encounter in Sivasagar on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

The encounter took place around 3.10 a.m. at Phulpanichiga under the Gaurisagar police station limits, when police were taking the accused, 34-year-old Ghanakanta Gogoi, from Guwahati to Sivasagar in connection with a 2024 bank fraud case registered in the…
On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), a Guwahati court sent Gogoi to judicial custody after his seven-day police remand in the hotel shootout case was completed.
Gogoi had been arrested within an hour of the October 26 shooting, which left five dead — Bhudev Bharali (65), Helena Bharali (58), Debarshi Kashyap (39), Rinika Kashyap (30) and Narayan Das (48).
Gogoi took the hotel from the Bharalis on a five-year lease on September 10, 2025, with the monthly rent reportedly fixed at ₹1.8 lakh.

items.title: Revanth asks officials to collect student feedback on school uniforms
points: Revanth Reddy at a review meeting on distribution of uniform and skill kits to students. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister A.

Revanth Reddy directed officials to collect feedback from students on the uniforms being distributed to them and to pay special attention to the colours and designs of the uniforms for future procurement.
The Chief Minister reviewed the distribution of uniforms and student kits to beneficiaries of government hostels, residential schools and government schools under various departments on Wednesday.

During the review meeting, officials informed the Chief Minister that the distribution of uniforms and essential student items, including ties, belts, identity cards, shoes, socks, plates, glasses, bowls, carpets and school bags, was almost complete.
They said that in a few institutions, the distribution of certain items had reached about 95%.
The Chief Minister also directed officials to prepare a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the procurement and distribution of uniforms and other student supplies for the next academic year.

items.title: AP High Court directs Vizianagaram SP to produce impersonator in forged land deed case
points: A Division Bench of the High Court comprising Justices Battu Devanand and Tuhin Kumar Gedela, directed the Vizianagaram District Superintendent of Police (SP) to secure and produce Pundari Mamata before the court.
Mamata is one of the respondents in a writ petition filed by Netula Sudharani, a resident of Vizianagaram.
The petitioner alleged that Mamata, a stranger to her, had fabricated a false death certificate claiming that Sudharani had died.
Mamata subsequently claimed to be her daughter and allegedly illegally obtained a forged legal heir certificate.

Using these forged documents, Mamata allegedly executed a fraudulent sale deed transferring a residential plot owned by Sudharani to one Ravi Kumar Naidu, who later mortgaged the property with Axis Bank.
Appearing for the petitioner, Senior Counsel S.S.
Prasad told the court that Mamata had failed to appear either in person or through her advocate in spite of repeated court notices.

items.title: BSE Q2 net profit rises 45% to ₹809 crore, revenue up 34%
points: The exchange’s net profit and revenue were, however, lower sequentially, declining 7.4 per cent and 8.5 per cent, respectively, from the June quarter.
Net profit in Q1 FY27 was ₹874.02 crore and revenue was ₹1,566.02 crore.
BSE recorded its highest-ever quarterly average daily turnover of ₹10,494 crore in the equity cash segment in Q2 FY27.
In index options, average daily premium turnover fell to ₹22,531 crore from ₹29,615 crore in Q1, due to lower volatility and temporary shifts in participation.
Its market share in monthly index options contracts was around 2-3 per cent, while that in non-expiry weeks was 6-7 per cent.
Co-location and other connectivity charges, including throttle charges, generated ₹103 crore in the first half of FY27.
BSE said its data centre had around 500 racks, all allocated, and it was building another 170-190 racks.
BSE’s EBITDA margin stood at 67-68 per cent, and management said a 65-70 per cent margin appeared sustainable.

items.title: Bengaluru: Poorly maintained civic work site turns Lower Agaram Road into accident hazard
points: Excavated soil has been piled up in multiple mounds along the stretch, while large stones have been left scattered haphazardly on the carriageway. | Photo Credit: ALLEN EGENUSE J.
Lower Agaram Road, a key connecting stretch in the southeastern part of the city, is lined with mounds of soil and piles of debris, posing a potential hazard to commuters.
Lower Agaram Road is a key route for residents of southeast Bengaluru travelling to the eastern and central parts of the city.
While Hosur Road was earlier the preferred route, increasing traffic congestion and ongoing Metro work over the years have led most residents to use Lower Agaram Road to reach central Bengaluru.
Vishwa Karanth, a regular commuter, said the sides of both carriageways had been dug up for over 20 days, while the scattered debris remained uncleared, slowing down traffic.
“When they closed a small portion about two months ago, it used to take over 15 minutes to cover a mere 2 km along the stretch.

items.title: Guntur intensifies chlorination of drinking water to prevent contamination after floods
points: The Rural Water Supply (RWS) Department has launched an extensive chlorination and super-chlorination drive across drinking water schemes in Guntur district to prevent contamination following floods triggered by Cyclone Murasu.
Acting on the advance instructions of District Collector C.M.
Saikanth Varma, the department initiated the measures on Wednesday immediately after the cyclone's intensity subsided.
Drinking water schemes in Nimmagadda Varipalem, Kantheru, Visadala, Mandapadu, Bheemuni Varipalem, Sowpadu, Narakoduru and Perecherla, among other villages, were covered under the programme.
Officials and field staff are thoroughly inspecting each water supply scheme to identify potential contamination and ensure the safety of drinking water.
Accordingly, all water supply schemes were filled to their full capacity in advance, and additional precautions were being taken to prevent contamination in the aftermath of the floods.
The department is taking all necessary steps to ensure the supply of safe drinking water to rural residents.

items.title: Hyderabad cybercrime police arrest 55 people in 38 cases across 7 States in October
points: The Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police arrested 55 people across seven States in October 2026 in connection with 38 cybercrime cases, while ₹49.99 lakh was refunded to victims during the month.

The arrests were made as part of special operations conducted by the Cyber Crime Police Station, Hyderabad City, following multiple complaints received through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP).

Of the 55 arrested, 20 were involved in trading fraud, 10 in OTP fraud, seven in social media-related offences, four each in investment fraud and business fraud, three each in digital arrest and APK fraud, two in miscellaneous cases, and one each in money…

Maharashtra and Telangana accounted for the highest number of arrests, with 16 each, followed by Andhra Pradesh with nine, Gujarat with seven, Delhi with five, and Haryana and Uttar Pradesh with one each.
Victims of trading fraud received ₹34.20 lakh, while ₹5.13 lakh was refunded in investment fraud cases.
The total amount lost across the 56 cases covered in the refund statement stood at ₹25.46 crore.

items.title: ₹146 crore for developing 13 camps affected by mining in Vijayanagara
points: During her visit to Jambunathahalli and Dalmia camps and other mining-affected areas, she inspected the living conditions and interacted with residents to hear their grievances.
The residents told her that despite living in the 13 camps for the past 50-60 years, they continue to lack proper housing and basic amenities.
They also described the difficult conditions during summer when some residents are forced to seek shelter in neighbouring forest areas to escape the scorching heat in the camps.
Responding to their grievances, Ms. Choudhary said that the State government has taken steps to ensure the comprehensive development of all 13 mining-affected camps with an allocation of ₹146 crore.

“Apart from infrastructure development, efforts will also be made to improve the socio-economic conditions of mining-affected families by creating opportunities for employment, education and skill development for the youth,” Ms. Choudhary said.
Ms. Choudhary made it clear that community halls in the camps should not be rented out for private functions or marriage ceremonies.

items.title: Unpaid for 10 months, vocational trainers in Telangana seek govt. intervention
points: Vocational trainers in schools across Telangana have raised an alarm over unpaid salaries for the past 10 months and appealed to Director of School Education E.
Naveen Nicolas to intervene and resolve their long-pending service-related grievances.
Representatives of the Telangana Vocational Trainers Association (TVTA) submitted a representation to Mr. Nicolas on Wednesday, highlighting the severe financial hardships faced by the trainers.
Vocational trainers are employed in the State Model Schools, Zilla Parishad High Schools, Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) and Gurukul institutions.
The association, in their representation, stated that the prolonged delay in salary payments had pushed hundreds of vocational trainers and their families into financial distress.

Despite their continued contribution to strengthening vocational education and imparting practical skills to students, the trainers alleged that their basic salary and service-related concerns remained unresolved.
They presented five demands to Mr. Nicolas for resolution.

items.title: Operation Toofan: 15,515 arrested, 14,369 cases registered in 5 months
points: Published - November 04, 2026 09:12 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Keralam Police have arrested 15,515 people and registered 14,369 cases during the first five months of Operation Toofan, the State-wide campaign launched to crackdown on drug trafficking…

Inspector General Putta Vimaladitya, the State nodal officer of Operation Toofan, who addressed a press conference here on Wednesday, said 1,173 people among those arrested have also been remanded in judicial custody.
The police seized 28.659 kg of MDMA and 1,960.139 kg of ganja during the operation.
The other confiscated substances included 7,261.352 g of hashish oil, 778.309 g of brown sugar, 1,226.678 g of methamphetamine, 673.076 g of heroin, 606.81 g of charas and 27.634 g of cocaine.
Of the cases registered, 193 involved commercial quantities of narcotic substances, while 638 concerned intermediate quantities.
Action was also initiated in 8,887 cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and 8,048 cases under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA).

items.title: Kunchacko Boban, Prithviraj named Keralam Forest dept. brand ambassadors
points: Published - November 04, 2026 09:10 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM Actors Kunchacko Boban and Prithviraj Sukumaran have been appointed brand ambassadors of the Forest department to promote forest conservation, wildlife protection and public participation in…
As brand ambassadors, the actors will promote awareness of forests, wildlife, biodiversity, habitat protection and ecological balance.
They will also support the promotion of departmental programmes, public services, conservation campaigns and citizen-participation initiatives.
The engagement will have a particular focus on children and young people.
The actors are expected to encourage students and young adults to develop an interest in nature through educational programmes, interactive sessions, nature camps and youth-oriented digital content.

Another important area of engagement will be promoting responsible behaviour towards wildlife, respect for forest-dependent communities, safe responses to wildlife encounters, and greater public participation in conservation efforts.
The actors will also support nature education and environmental literacy programmes aimed at improving public understanding of ecosystems, biodiversity and ecological relationships.

items.title: Chikkajala Fort to get a new lease of life after a decade under CSR funds
points: A ceremony was recently held at the fort to mark the beginning of the project, with Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda in attendance, along with members of Intach and Kashi Ra, the organisation funding the project.

The fort includes a small Anjaneya Swamy Temple, where a daily puja is performed by a local priest, and kalyani and stone mantapas on two acres under survey number 116, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Revenue Department.
These were built in the 19th century, inspired by the Vijayanagara style, and used as a ‘chatra’ or rest stops for soldiers, businesspersons, and others professions who travelled long distances.

The stones in the kalyani and mantapa feature carvings of nagabhanda, elephant, shivalinga, purnakumba and anjaneya, fishes, birds and a few others, said a senior official from the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage.
When The Hindu visited Chikkajala Fort, huge trees and bushes had grown inside the mantapa.

items.title: SEBI relaxes KYC rules for NRIs, OCIs: Can overseas investors now onboard digitally from abroad? Decoded
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has relaxed Know Your Client (KYC) requirements for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs), and foreign nationals, allowing them to complete digital onboarding while residing…

In a circular dated November 4, 2026, the market regulator said individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs) located in countries compliant with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) can submit their KYC information and supporting documents digitally…

The move removes the earlier requirement that clients must be physically present in India while completing digital KYC, which had effectively restricted investors residing overseas from completing the onboarding process remotely.
The revised framework will come into effect from December 3, 2026, or 30 days from the date of the circular.
Foreign nationals can provide government-issued documents or a letter from a foreign embassy or mission in India if their identity documents do not mention their address, according to SEBI circular.
Where physical verification is not feasible, intermediaries can conduct Video In-Person Verification (VIPV).

items.title: 14 second-year MBBS students at GMC Kamareddy suspended for ragging juniors
points: Fourteen second-year MBBS students of the Government Medical College (GMC), Kamareddy, have been suspended following a ragging complaint lodged with the National Medical Commission (NMC).
Valya, the college received a complaint forwarded by the NMC based on a representation from freshers.
Explaining the circumstances surrounding the incident, he said freshers and final-year students were accommodated in a common hostel.
The second-year students, who were not residing in the college hostel, had entered an unauthorised area of the hostel and were caught on the college campus.
A student offered a different account of the incident, claiming that the complaint stemmed from seniors expecting juniors to greet them frequently with ‘good morning’ wishes.
Following the complaint, the college’s anti-ragging committee conducted an inquiry and initiated disciplinary action against the students involved.
Four students have been suspended for six months, while 10 others have been given a four-month suspension.
The college is also preparing to submit an action-taken report to the NMC, Dr Valya added.

items.title: Fire NOC rules eased for existing schools and colleges in Telangana
points: The revised guidelines, announced by DG of Fire Services Vikram Singh Mann, will apply to NOC applications received on or after November 10.
Under the revised provisions, educational institutions can retain the existing open spaces available within their premises without being required to create additional open spaces.

Where existing setbacks are deficient, water curtains must be installed on the affected sides that do not have an adjoining road as a compensatory measure to prevent fire from spreading from neighbouring properties.
A four-way fire brigade inlet must also be provided.
The guidelines also clarify requirements for providing a second staircase in existing educational buildings, taking into account their height and configuration.

These include fire extinguishers, modular sprinklers in applicable chemical laboratories and computer laboratories or server rooms, first-aid hose reels, manually operated electronic fire alarm systems, downcomers, overhead firefighting water storage tanks…

items.title: HC hears plea against Google data centre, says project is subject to its decision on Writ Petition
points: A man walking past a banner displayed on AI Data Centers in Visakhapatnam.
Construction of Google data centre has been met with resistance from residents.
The Bench, however, did not go into the merits of the case due to paucity of time as it was dealing with some time-sensitive petitions related to NEET admissions.

The petitioner’s counsel Virag Gupta, insisted that VHDCPL was carrying out construction of the data centre in the prohibited, eco-sensitive zone of Kambalakonda.

Besides, he contended that the 30-year lease granted for non-temple industrial purposes was illegal, and urged the court to record an interim restraint against any construction activity within one kilometre distance of the Kambalakonda wildlife sanctuary.

“The government at the time sought to safeguard lives on the roads by prohibiting dangerous vehicle modifications, installing AI-monitored cameras, and enforcing rigorous, uncompromising inspections.

“It is pointless for those who played politics with people’s lives to shed crocodile tears now.
Having sacrificed the State’s road safety for cheap political gains, they must now correct their course and demonstrate a sincere commitment to the enforcement of the law,” he said.

items.title: MP high court rejects bail plea of ex-judge Giribala Singh in Twisha Sharma case
points: Madhya Pradesh high court rejected the bail plea of former district and sessions judge Giribala Singh in the suicide case of model Twisha Sharma, after a marathon hearing.
